name: Unfilled Order Ledger
note: Not a signal - an order-type experiment. The signal set is frozen (20-bar Donchian breaks) and only the arm changes: 0 takes the next open, 1 rests a limit k ATR back and simply never trades if it is not touched within n_life bars, 2 rests the same limit and chases at market when it expires. Exits are identical across arms (2 ATR stop, 3 ATR target, 40-bar time stop), so comparing arm 1 with arm 0 over the identical signal dates prices the opportunity cost of the unfilled orders - they are missing from arm 1 and present in arm 0. Honest limitation: the harness fills at the next open, so arm 1 gets the touch bars successor open rather than the limit price itself, which understates the price improvement and leaves only the adverse-selection half of the effect.
source: Perold (1988), 'The Implementation Shortfall: Paper versus Reality', Journal of Portfolio Management 14(3):4-9 - the delay/execution/opportunity-cost decomposition. The adverse selection framing of resting limit orders is standard market microstructure.
code:
def family_init(ctx):
    """One frozen signal, three order types.

    The signal set is Donchian(20) breakouts and never changes. What changes is
    HOW the order reaches the market: arm 0 takes the next open, arm 1 rests a
    limit k*ATR back and simply never trades if it is not touched within N
    bars, arm 2 rests the same limit and chases at market when it expires.
    Comparing arm 1 against arm 0 over the identical signal dates is the whole
    experiment: arm 1 is missing exactly the trades that ran away from it, and
    that omission is the opportunity cost the study is trying to price.
    """
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    hi = [float(b["h"]) for b in bars]
    lo = [float(b["l"]) for b in bars]
    cl = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]

    arm = int(ctx.p.arm)
    k = float(ctx.p.limit_atr)
    life = max(1, int(ctx.p.n_life))
    w = max(2, int(ctx.p.don))
    both = int(ctx.p.both_sides) != 0

    # Wilder ATR(14), computed here because family_init cannot index a series
    per = max(2, int(ctx.p.atr_n))
    atr = [None] * n
    s = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        tr = hi[i] - lo[i] if i == 0 else max(hi[i] - lo[i],
                                              abs(hi[i] - cl[i - 1]),
                                              abs(lo[i] - cl[i - 1]))
        if i < per:
            s += tr
            if i == per - 1:
                atr[i] = s / per
        else:
            atr[i] = (atr[i - 1] * (per - 1) + tr) / per

    sig = [0] * n

    def _stamp(i, d):
        if sig[i] == 0:
            sig[i] = d

    for t in range(w, n):
        a = atr[t]
        if a is None or a <= 0:
            continue
        up = cl[t] > max(hi[t - w:t])
        dn = both and cl[t] < min(lo[t - w:t])
        if not up and not dn:
            continue
        d = 1 if up else -1
        if arm <= 0:                                   # arm A: market
            _stamp(t, d)
            continue
        lim = cl[t] - k * a * d                        # arm B / C: resting limit
        hit = None
        for u in range(t + 1, min(n, t + 1 + life)):
            if (lo[u] <= lim) if d > 0 else (hi[u] >= lim):
                hit = u
                break
        if hit is not None:
            _stamp(hit, d)
        elif arm >= 2:                                 # expired: chase
            u = min(n - 1, t + life)
            _stamp(u, d)

    ctx.sig = ctx.series(sig, "arm_signal")


def signal(ctx, i):
    return ctx.sig[i]
